key.text: I want to make a phone stand for my desk out of wood. It should hold my phone at a slight angle, fit in my hand, and I only need one.

output.summary: A small wooden phone stand that holds your phone at an angle.

needs.why: Cut flat wooden pieces that slot together
Or print the stand in one piece

routes.process: Cut flat pieces from plywood and slot them together.
routes.fit_reason: Slotted plywood is quick to cut and needs no glue. It is a good first project on the laser cutter.

steps.title: Sketch the pieces
steps.detail: Draw the stand as two or three flat pieces that slot together. Keep slots the same width as the plywood.

steps.title: Take Level 1 training
steps.detail: Do the Level 1 orientation and safety training before using the laser cutter (cuts flat sheets very precisely).

steps.title: Make a cardboard test
steps.detail: Cut the shapes from cardboard first to check the angle and fit with your phone.

steps.title: Cut and assemble
steps.detail: Cut the final pieces from plywood and slide them together. Sand any rough edges.

warnings.issue: Slots that are too tight or too loose
warnings.fix: Measure the plywood thickness and test a single slot in cardboard first.

routes.process: Print the whole stand in one piece from plastic.
routes.fit_reason: Printing needs no assembly and the printer does the hard part. It takes a few hours, so plan ahead.

steps.title: Find or draw a model
steps.detail: Search for a free phone stand model, or draw a simple wedge shape.

steps.title: Take Level 1 training
steps.detail: Do the Level 1 orientation and safety training first.

steps.title: Prepare the file
steps.detail: Ask staff to help you slice the model (turn it into printer instructions).

steps.title: Print and check
steps.detail: Start the print, check the first layer sticks, and collect it when done.

warnings.fix: Make the back support at least 4 mm thick.
